title: The booking appointment
blurb: Book by 10+0 weeks, take a full history, carry out the booking measurements and bloods, offer screening and complete the risk assessments that shape the whole pregnancy.
question: Ngozi, 41, is 8+3 weeks pregnant with her first baby. Her BMI is 36 kg/m² and her mother has type 2 diabetes. What must the booking midwife assess, and what will the plan include?

teach.h: The appointment that shapes the pregnancy
teach.body: Booking is the first antenatal appointment with a midwife. NICE NG201 aims for it by 10+0 weeks so that screening, supplements and risk-reducing treatment can start in time. The midwife takes a full history, measures and tests, offers screening, and completes risk assessments that decide whether care stays midwife-led or needs obstetric input. In plain English: everything that happens later is planned from what is found today, in partnership with the woman (SPM 3.22, 3.23).

steps.label: Referral
steps.sub: Self, GP, midwife or community route

steps.label: Booking by 10+0
steps.sub: Face to face with a midwife

teach.caption: Late booking can signal social risk (NG201 1.1.6). Give her a schedule of appointments and an out-of-hours number.

head: Area
Ask about
rows: Past or current illness; Whooley and GAD-2
Prescribed, over the counter, herbal; allergies
Occupation, home, support, smoking, alcohol, drugs

head: Item
Detail
rows: FBC, blood group and RhD status
IDPS, sickle cell and thalassaemia, FASP
teach.caption: She may accept or decline any part of any screening programme (NG201 1.2.13).

head: Risk
If present
rows: OGTT at 24–28 weeks (earlier if previous GDM)
Growth surveillance plan; repeat in 2nd trimester

root.label: Any risk factor?
root.sub: BMI 30+, baby 4.5 kg+, previous GDM, first-degree relative with diabetes, high-prevalence ethnicity

children.label: Early testing after booking
children.sub: Plus OGTT at 24–28 wks if normal

teach.caption: Do not use urine glucose, random or fasting glucose, HbA1c or glucose challenge to assess GDM risk.

teach.body: Folic acid 400 micrograms daily to 12 weeks; 5 mg only for specific risks such as diabetes, a previous neural tube defect or anti-epileptic medicines (NICE NG247). Vitamin D 10 micrograms daily from October to March, or all year if she is at increased risk of deficiency (NG247 1.1.12). VTE risk is assessed at booking and after any admission; women at risk are referred to an obstetrician. Under the RCOG position statement (September 2026), a booking BMI of 50 or more means LMWH through pregnancy and for 6 weeks after birth.
teach.cite: NICE NG247 1.1.5–1.1.7, 1.1.12; NG201 1.2.18–1.2.20; RCOG GTG 37a position statement Sept 2026

teach.body: Ngozi's BMI 36 and her mother's type 2 diabetes are GDM risk factors, so an OGTT is planned at 24–28 weeks. For pre-eclampsia she has three moderate factors (first pregnancy, age 40+, BMI 35+), so aspirin 75–150 mg daily from 12 weeks is advised and prescribed. BMI alone does not need 5 mg folic acid, so 400 micrograms continues. Her VTE score is calculated and she is referred to an obstetrician if at risk.

teach.text: Since NICE NG247 (2025), a BMI of 30 or more on its own NO LONGER means 5 mg folic acid: 400 micrograms unless a specific risk (such as diabetes) applies. And a 'glucose 1+' on her urine dipstick is not a GDM risk assessment.

items.label: to book if she contacts after 9+0

items: Book by 10+0 weeks; within 2 weeks if she makes contact after 9+0; ask why if she books late.
Full history including mental health, medicines, family, social circumstances, domestic abuse (alone) and FGM.
Height, weight, BMI; FBC, blood group and RhD; BP with a validated device; urine dipstick; CO test.
Offer IDPS, SCT and FASP screening and a dating scan at 11+2 to 14+1; each is her choice.
Assess GDM, pre-eclampsia, FGR and VTE risk and act: OGTT, aspirin, growth plan, obstetric referral.

summary: You can now organise a booking appointment from referral to risk plan: history, measurements, bloods, screening offers and the GDM, pre-eclampsia, FGR and VTE assessments. You can also give correct folic acid advice under NICE NG247 and act on each risk you find.

A.q: According to NICE NG201, by what gestation should the booking appointment ideally take place?
A.why: NG201 1.1.4: offer a booking appointment with a midwife to take place by 10+0 weeks.

whyNot.0: 8+0 weeks is earlier than the NICE standard.
whyNot.2: 12+6 weeks is a commissioning data point (CG110), not the booking target.
whyNot.3: 14+1 weeks is the end of the dating scan window.

A.q: Which blood tests does NICE NG201 list for the first face-to-face antenatal appointment?
options: FBC, blood group and RhD status
A.why: NG201 1.2.12: offer a blood test to check full blood count, blood group and rhesus D status (with IDPS and SCT screening offered separately).

whyNot.0: Ferritin and vitamin D are not routine booking tests in NG201.
whyNot.1: HbA1c and TSH are not routine booking bloods.
whyNot.2: Fasting glucose is not used to assess GDM risk at booking (NG3).

A.q: Within which window should the dating scan be offered?
A.why: NG201 1.2.14: offer a scan between 11+2 and 14+1 weeks to determine gestational age, detect multiple pregnancy and, if chosen, screen for trisomies.

whyNot.0: This is earlier than the dating scan window.
whyNot.2: This is after the window closes.
whyNot.3: 18+0 to 20+6 is the anomaly scan window.

B.q: Which booking finding is a NICE NG3 risk factor for gestational diabetes?
B.why: NG3 1.2.2: risk factors are BMI of 30 kg/m² or over, previous baby 4.5 kg or more, previous GDM, a first-degree relative with diabetes, and family origin with a high prevalence of diabetes.

whyNot.0: The NG3 threshold is a previous baby of 4.5 kg or more.
whyNot.2: Urine glucose is not used to assess GDM risk.
whyNot.3: Age is not one of the NG3 GDM risk factors.

B.q: Elif contacts the maternity service for the first time at 11 weeks. What should happen?
options: Book her within 2 weeks and ask about the delay
Book her at the routine 16-week appointment
Wait for her dating scan result before booking
Ask her GP to complete the booking for her
B.why: NG201 1.1.5–1.1.6: if contact is after 9+0 weeks, offer booking within 2 weeks if possible, and ask about the reasons for booking late.

whyNot.1: Waiting until 16 weeks delays screening and risk assessment.
whyNot.2: Booking should not wait for the scan; both should happen promptly.

B.q: Hannah, 7 weeks pregnant, has a BMI of 38 and no other risk factors for neural tube defects. Which folic acid advice is correct?
options: No folic acid now she is pregnant
B.why: NICE NG247 1.1.6: a BMI of 25 kg/m² or more does not on its own need more than 400 micrograms; take it daily until 12 weeks.

whyNot.0: 5 mg is for specific risks such as diabetes or a previous NTD, not BMI alone.
whyNot.1: High-dose folic acid is not advised throughout pregnancy for BMI.
whyNot.3: Folic acid continues until 12 weeks even if not started before conception.

C.q: Ngozi, 41, is in her first pregnancy with a BMI of 36. She has no chronic illness. What pre-eclampsia prevention should the midwife advise?
options: No aspirin, as she has no high-risk factor
C.why: NG133 1.1.3: more than one moderate factor (here nulliparity, age 40+, BMI 35+) means aspirin 75–150 mg daily from 12 weeks until birth, prescribed.

whyNot.0: Two or more moderate risk factors also qualify for aspirin.
whyNot.1: The dose is 75–150 mg and it starts from 12 weeks.
whyNot.2: Aspirin starts from 12 weeks and continues until birth.

C.q: At booking, Mel's BMI is 52 kg/m². Under the RCOG position statement of September 2026, what VTE prophylaxis plan is advised?
options: LMWH antenatally and for 6 weeks after birth
Compression stockings and review at 36 weeks
Low-dose aspirin to reduce clot risk
C.why: RCOG position statement amending GTG 37a (Sept 2026): a booking BMI of 50 or more means LMWH antenatally and for 6 weeks postnatally. NG201 1.2.20: refer to an obstetrician.

whyNot.1: Postnatal-only prophylaxis falls short of the antenatal and 6-week plan for BMI 50+.
whyNot.2: Stockings alone and late review do not meet the statement.
whyNot.3: Aspirin is for pre-eclampsia prevention, not VTE prophylaxis.

C.q: Which mental health questions does NICE CG192 recommend asking every woman at booking?
C.why: CG192 1.5.4: at booking and early postnatally, ask the two Whooley depression questions and the GAD-2 anxiety questions.

whyNot.0: The EPDS is used as part of further assessment after a positive screen.
whyNot.2: PHQ-9 is a further assessment tool, not the booking screen.
whyNot.3: GAD-7 follows a GAD-2 score of 3 or more.

reteach.title: History, measure, offer, assess
reteach.question: Can you run booking as four blocks so nothing is missed?

blocks.body: HISTORY: medical, obstetric, family, mental health, medicines, social, and alone-time questions about abuse and FGM. MEASURE: height, weight, BMI, BP, urine, CO, FBC, group and RhD. OFFER: IDPS, SCT, FASP, dating scan. ASSESS: GDM, pre-eclampsia, FGR, VTE, then act on each.

blocks.text: BMI 30+ alone does not mean 5 mg folic acid any more (NICE NG247).

explain.body: Book by 10+0 weeks. If she first makes contact after 9+0, book within 2 weeks if possible. If she books late, ask why.

test.q: A woman books at 19 weeks. What does NICE NG201 say the midwife should do?
options: Ask about the reasons for booking late
Decline the dating scan and screening
test.why: NG201 1.1.6: if a woman books late, ask about the reasons; late booking can reflect social risk.

whyNot.1: Screening and scans are still offered as appropriate to gestation.
whyNot.2: She still needs midwifery antenatal care.
whyNot.3: There is no reason to delay further.

explain.body: Medical, obstetric and family history (both biological parents), mental health, medicines including herbal and over the counter, allergies, occupation, home and support, and private questions about abuse and FGM.

test.q: Whose family history does NICE NG201 ask the midwife to take at booking?
options: The woman's side of the family
Both biological parents of the baby
The baby's grandparents on both sides
test.why: NG201 1.2.1: ask about family history of both biological parents.

whyNot.0: The other biological parent's history matters too.
whyNot.2: The partner present may not be the biological parent.
whyNot.3: The focus is the biological parents' family history.

explain.body: Height, weight, BMI; FBC, blood group and RhD; BP with a validated device; urine dipstick; CO test. Offer IDPS, SCT and FASP screening; each part can be accepted or declined.

test.q: Which statement about booking screening is correct?
options: She must accept all screening at booking
She can accept or decline any part of it
Declining one test means declining all
Screening waits until the dating scan
test.why: NG201 1.2.13: inform the woman she can accept or decline any part of any of the screening programmes offered.

whyNot.2: Each part is a separate choice.
whyNot.3: IDPS and SCT are offered at booking.

explain.body: GDM (OGTT at 24–28 weeks if at risk), pre-eclampsia (aspirin from 12 weeks), FGR (repeat in second trimester), VTE (refer if at risk; BMI 50+ means LMWH antenatally and 6 weeks postnatally).

test.q: A woman's sister has type 1 diabetes. What GDM plan does NICE NG3 advise?
options: No testing, as it is not a risk
test.why: A first-degree relative with diabetes is an NG3 risk factor, so offer a 75 g OGTT at 24–28 weeks.

whyNot.0: Urine glucose is not used to assess GDM risk.
whyNot.1: HbA1c is not used to assess GDM risk.
whyNot.2: A first-degree relative with diabetes is a recognised risk factor.
